claim: An estimated 53.2 million US adults aged 18 or older reported diagnosed arthritis in the combined 2019–2021 NHIS; this is not a count of hand arthritis or potential users.
CDC FastStats reports diagnosed arthritis among 21.1% of US adults aged 18 or older in 2025 (NHIS). This is not hand-specific and should not be multiplied by an unrelated population total.

A 2026 study using 2023 NHIS data estimated that 24.8 million US adults with doctor-diagnosed arthritis reported activity limitations attributable to arthritis. This does not measure hand limitations specifically.

A 2025 conference abstract analyzing NHANES reported difficulty grasping or handling small objects among 25.1% of men and 34.9% of women aged 65 or older in 2021–2023. Preliminary abstract evidence; not all US adults or a causal COVID estimate.
WHO's January 2024 fact sheet reports that more than 2.5 billion people globally need at least one assistive product across all categories, not specifically hand aids.
